Special Agents Charles Kunkel and Maurice Miller wrote this Secret Service report in November and December 1963. It is numbered CO-2-34,030 and comes from the Dallas office. Its subject is protective research into the assassination of President Kennedy: the service's own study of how its protection had failed.

Protective research was the branch meant to learn from threats before they succeeded. After Dallas, it studied the worst failure in the service's history. Kunkel and Miller's report belongs to the first weeks of that reckoning. It preserves the service examining itself while the Warren Commission was still being formed, a primary record of an agency asking what it had missed.
